title: Swedish women grab world hockey bronze from Finland, its first medal at tourney since 2007
summary: Hilda Svensson scored the decisive shootout goal and Sweden medalled at the women's world hockey championship for the first time since 2007 by defeating Finland 2-1 in the bronze medal final on…

image.caption: Sweden rallied from a 1-0 deficit to beat Finland for the bronze medal at the women's world hockey championship on Monday in Herning, Denmark. Lina Ljungblom and Hilda Svensson, in the shootout, had the goals. (Ida Marie Odgaard/Ritzau Scanpix/AFP via Getty Images)

blocks.text: Hilda Svensson scored the decisive shootout goal and Sweden medalled at the women's world hockey championship for the first time since 2007 by defeating Finland 2-1 in the bronze medal final on Monday in Herning, Denmark.
Canada battles defending champions U.S. later Monday in Denmark

Hilda Svensson scored the decisive shootout goal and Sweden medalled at the women’s world hockey championship for the first time since 2007 by defeating Finland 2-1 in the bronze medal final on Monday in Herning, Denmark.

Sweden rallied from a 1-0 deficit with Lina Ljungblom tying the score with a power-play goal from the slot with six minutes left in regulation. Svensson, a 20-year-old sophomore at Ohio State, had an assist on Ljungblom’s goal.

Svensson then scored Sweden’s second shootout goal by driving in from the right wing and beating Sanni Ahola with a snapshot inside the far post. Ebba Svensson Traff sealed the win by stopping Finland’s final two attempts, including a right pad save on Emmi Juusela.
Defending world and Olympic champion United States was scheduled to face rival Canada in the gold-medal contest at 1 p.m. ET.
Svensson Traff stopped 29 shots through overtime and four of five shootout attempts.

Michelle Karvinen opened the scoring with a power-play goal with 3:05 left in the second period, and Noora Tulus scored Finland’s lone shootout goal. The 36-year-old Karvinen's goal was her team career record 27th in world championship play, moving her one ahead of Petra Nieminen.

items: Canada tops Sweden, advancing to gold-medal game against U.S.

blocks.text: Ahola finished with 35 saves through overtime and allowed a shootout goal by Tilde Grillfors.
Sweden was making its first tournament medal-game appearance since a 4-1 loss to Finland in 2009. Sweden won its third medal after also winning bronze in 2005.
The Swedes were coming off a promising fourth-place finish at the Milano-Cortina Olympics in February in which they lost the bronze-medal final to Switzerland.
